newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares firm 0.62 pct despite politic fears.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares firm 0.62 pct despite politic fears.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed on Friday after Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller denied a press report that she would pull out of the Islamist-led coalition, brokers said.
But they said worries about the future of the government persisted as the market awaited Saturday's National Security Council (NSC) meeting to set direction next week.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,466, up nine points, or 0.62 percent from Thursday when it sank 4.9 percent following a 6-1/2 day holiday.

"Official statements on the continuation of the government enlivened trade slightly in the afternoon. But the market trend depends on the results of the NSC meeting," said Koray Cervatoglu from Baran securities.
The index had eased 0.21 percent to 1,454 in the morning.
Ciller denied a newspaper report that she had decided to pull her conservative DYP out of the 10-month-old coalition.
The DYP is uneasy due to Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's failure to implement an anti-Islamist crackdown demanded by the secularist army at a February 28 NSC meeting.
